<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json da6f0ce35da60bf81e79890b227815a989f9b165` → `packageMentionDocs`.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

Scope: docs/adr/0120-unique-scope-vocabulary-and-null-safe-tenant-uniqueness.md + content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx, packages/qa/dogfood/test/create-caller-id-collision.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/create-caller-id-collision-walled.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/vitest.config.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts, packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/duplicate-record-error.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/core/src/security/tenant-layer0-verdict.ts, packages/verify/src/harness.ts, scripts/adr-index.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml

Per the 2026-10-29 security-hardening disclosure ruling this record names positions and contracts only.

### ① Derived judgments

Face: governed rules text (`docs/adr/**`). No published schema moves; no product code moves. Each accept-set or public-surface claim the diff makes, judged:

1. **Status line — right.** `**Status**: Accepted (…) · **Amended** (2026-11-01, …)` keeps `Accepted` as the parsed keyword (`scripts/adr-index.mjs` takes the EARLIEST keyword in the value, `statusKeywordOf`), which is the register's form for an in-force record with an amendment (ADR-0005, ADR-0009 use the same `· Amended` suffix). The index cell truncates at 64 characters before the new text, so `docs/adr/README.md` is not stale; the dev's `check:adr-index` exit 0 agrees.
2. **Amendment form — right.** A dated blockquote `> **Amendment (date, ref) — …**` under the business-requirement matrix is this ADR's own existing form (the 2026-08-22 amendment at its line 356) and the register's (ADR-0131 line 248, ADR-0090 lines 677/738 use the same `> **Amended (date, ruling of record …)**` shape). AGENTS.md PD 13 asks for a new ADR or an amended status line; the PR does the latter plus the pointer in the S10 row. Sanctioned.
3. **Ruling fidelity — right, and no more.** The note states exactly: S10's no-oracle promise is scoped to `'organization'` uniqueness (and field-level `true`, its synonym); `id` is the one deployment-global key; a create colliding on it answers one refusal, identical for visible, in-organization-hidden and cross-organization holders, naming no organization or owner; the signal is bounded by id unguessability. It cites rule 2 of `5934879010` verbatim where it binds (no new code, no detail naming the holder's organization) and records the 2026-11-01 extension from upsert to every create door and to the same-organization half. Ruling `5985885287` is left untouched with the correct reason (a held id has no "nonexistent" answer to give). Rejected options a–e are recorded as rejected, not promised.
4. **S10 scoping claim — right.** `id` is not a scoped `unique` declaration; the primary key is materialized verbatim under every posture and no `COALESCE(organization_id, …)` key part reaches it (D3 governs declared `'organization'` indexes and field-level `unique`, not the PK). The amendment's cross-reference to §Posture portability ("becomes a cross-customer existence oracle (S10)" for a `'global'` unique, ADR line 206) is the same oracle, accurately cited.
5. **Entropy claim — right.** `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts:266` `DEFAULT_ID_LENGTH = 16`, minted by `nanoid(DEFAULT_ID_LENGTH)` at its three mint sites (6463, 8216, 8629); nanoid's default alphabet is 64 symbols, so 16 characters = 96 bits. The importer pre-assigns `randomUUID()` when the row carries none (`packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:1243`, "An id the user supplied explicitly is respected"). The pins' `freshId` (12 random bytes, base64url) reproduces the minted shape.
6. **Door inventory — each door's answer read in code:**
   - `POST /data/:object`: `engine.insert` honours a caller `id`; the driver's primary-key violation leaves the engine as the #14095 `DuplicateRecordError` envelope (engine.ts ~15993) and the HTTP mapping answers `409` `{ error: 'A record with this value already exists', code: 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION', developerMessage, field?, object }` (`data-error-classification.ts:1058-1075`). `developerMessage` is `buildDuplicateMessage(objectLabel, fieldLabel)` — object and field only, never a value, owner or organization — so the body is identical across holders. **Right.**
   - `POST /data/:object/batch` `operation: 'create'`: the row's `errors[0].code` is `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` and `httpStatus` reads the declared 409 (protocol.ts 3533 docblock). **Right.**
   - cross-object `POST /batch`: one engine transaction, rolled back on the first failing operation (http-protocol.mdx Batch section, unchanged). **Right.**
   - `createMany` (`POST /data/:object/createMany`, `rest-server.zod.ts:601`): `createManyData` is one `engine.insert(object, records[])`; on driver-sql the batch is one multi-row `bulkCreate` statement (sql-driver.ts 8616 docblock: "the batch is ALREADY all-or-nothing"), so a collision answers a whole-request 409 and writes nothing there. **Right on the persistent SQL drivers; see 7.**
   - import `insert`: no existence lookup (`writeMode !== 'insert'` gates `findExisting`), the supplied id is respected and a collision is the row's `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` (`import-runner.ts:539`). import `upsert`: `findExisting` runs through `findArgsBase`, which spreads the caller's `context` (830-834), by `matchFields`; a miss creates. "An upsert whose match, run as the caller, finds no row creates" — **right.**
   - clone `overrides.id`: `CLONE_STRIP_FIELDS` strips the source `id`, overrides are assigned after the strip (protocol.ts 14255-14300), and the same `engine.insert` honours it. **Right.**
7. **Wrong by omission (should-fix, not must-fix): the store precondition.** The note's facts — "answers `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION` and writes nothing" — are stated for every door without naming the store. `driver-memory` enforces no primary key (memory-driver.ts:476 docblock; `create()` stores `data.id || generateId`, line 845): a create naming a held id lands a second row there, on every door. Ruling `5934879010` itself put driver-memory out of scope. The binding sentence (no visibility-shaped answer, no holder named) still holds on that store, so this is a qualifier the record owes, not a false promise about a production door: one clause, "on a store that enforces the primary key — every persistent driver; `driver-memory` declares none". The same clause covers the engine's own note that a driver without a statement-level transaction may apply a `createMany` batch partially (engine.ts ~15985).
8. **Sibling consistency (should-fix on whichever lands second).** The note lists the create doors and names import's upsert arm as a create door; it does not name `POST /data/:object/batch` `operation: 'upsert'`. On `main` today that door forks on system-context existence (`probeRecord`, protocol-batch-data.ts 353), so a hidden held id takes the UPDATE arm and never creates — the note is accurate for `main`. `claude/harden-upsert-by-id-visibility` (changeset `batch-upsert-by-id-caller-read.md`, patch, `Clause-②: no`) makes an unreadable row take the INSERT arm, "so the row answers exactly as a `create` naming that `id` answers", and its code comment cites this 2026-11-01 extension as its record. After it lands the note is incomplete, not contradicted. The door belongs in the list under the same parenthetical as import's upsert; adding it now would describe `main` falsely, so: the later of the two PRs adds the sentence.
9. **http-protocol.mdx Create Record paragraph + 409 example — right.** Status, code, body keys and the unnamed sentence match the mapping in 6. `field: "id"` is best-effort as the paragraph says (SQLite's `constraint failed: table.id` and Postgres's `Key (id)=` parse to the column; MySQL's `for key 'PRIMARY'` does not) and the paragraph defers to the Delete section's Constraint Violations note on that, consistently. "A create never overwrites — change an existing record with Update Record" is consistent with the Update paragraph's #2948 rule (`id` is read-only on update, honoured on create). The 405/400 sections are untouched and not contradicted. Anchors `#update-record`, `#delete-record`, `#batch-operations` resolve to existing headings; Check Documentation Links is green. The example omits `developerMessage`, as every existing 409 example on the page does — a convention, not drift.
10. **Pins — non-vacuous, and they prove what they claim.** Each file: a PRECONDITION case measures the hiding (the caller / B reads the held row as 404, the owner / A and the operator read it as 200, both rows in one organization or in two distinct ones with the stamped `organization_id` asserted); a CONTROL per door proves a fresh caller `id` lands as given with the expected owner / organization; the identity case asserts `refusalCode(onOwn) === 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION'` FIRST (so two undefined bodies cannot pass), then same status, `toEqual` on the whole body, and byte-identical rows after via `JSON.stringify` of system-context reads; the naming case asserts the body contains none of org ids, slugs, user ids, emails, nor the four key spellings. Per-object batch asserts `httpStatus: 409` and `succeeded: 0`.
11. **Walled boot — the wall is real on this boot; the dev's docblock flag is confirmed.** `multiTenant: 'posture-only'` registers only the `org-scoping` stand-in (harness.ts 1090-1102). The stamp is the engine's `injectTenantOnInsert` ("keeps the active organization as `tenantId` in EVERY posture", engine.ts ~7341) and the wall is the Layer-0 verdict off `tenancy.posture` (`postureEnforcesWall`, tenant-layer0-verdict.ts:131), which the stand-in makes non-degraded `isolated` — neither lives in the service the docblock says is absent. So the harness docblock (harness.ts 77-80, 248-257: "stamps no `organization_id` and scopes no query … would assert nothing and pass") is stale since ADR-0131 D8/D11. The pin does not lean on it: the precondition measures the 404 and would FAIL on an unwalled boot. See ③.
12. **vitest.config — right.** The same-organization file joins the `shared-showcase` exact list; the walled file falls to the `isolated` glob project (derived population, no second list to keep in step).
13. **Disclosure — right.** ADR, page and pin prose name doors, codes and contracts; the only "recipe" is the public API's documented behaviour.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset`, no changeset — **correct.** The diff touches `docs/adr/**`, `content/docs/**` and `packages/qa/dogfood/**` (`"private": true`); nothing publishes from a released package, which is exactly what AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 reserves the label for. No `Clause-②:` line is owed by a diff that declares no published change; `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green on the head. Check-runs at reading: no failure; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Build Core`, `Test Core 5-8`, `Type Check · source gates / debt ledger`, Lint scoped families green; `Type Check · workspace / consumer gates`, `Test Core 1-4`, `Lint · repo & tooling / docs & code guards / CI, release & engine gates`, `Build Docs` still in progress — landing waits for green per the seat's ② gate, this record does not.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag — harness docblock drift: confirmed (①.11).** Not this PR's scope (`packages/verify` is a published package; a docblock correction is its own patch). Card it: `BootOptions.multiTenant` and `SimulatedOrgScopingPlugin` docblocks in `packages/verify/src/harness.ts` describe a pre-ADR-0131 world; the honest sentence is that the stand-in flips the posture and the engine's stamp plus the Layer-0 verdict then wall by posture — the proof the docblock says does not exist here now does.
- **Dev flag — unpinned doors (`createMany`, import insert/upsert, clone `overrides.id`): answered.** Read in code (①.6); each answers the collision as the ADR states on the persistent drivers. They stay unpinned; a low-priority follow-up pin card is reasonable, not owed before landing.
- **Dev open question — fleet-write `pr_create` read-back prints no labels line: out of scope.** PM tooling, not this PR. The labels are on the PR as read over REST (`documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `skip-changeset`); nothing on this PR depends on the read-back.
- **CI shape the seat should know:** the dogfood shards are skipped on `pull_request` by design (ci.yml `dogfood` job `if:` excludes `pull_request` and `merge_group`; `dogfood-gate` is the always-run aggregator). The pins' only evidence at this head is the dev's local run (2 files, 30 cases, verify-lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`); CI runs them on the push to `main`. Repo-standard, not a defect of this PR.
- **Sibling ordering (①.8):** `claude/harden-upsert-by-id-visibility` is in flight on the same ruling; whichever lands second adds the per-object batch `upsert` door to the ADR note's list. The seat holds the ordering.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` — no login note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

`docs/adr/0120-unique-scope-vocabulary-and-null-safe-tenant-uniqueness.md`, against its first consumer and its execution plan:

- **First consumer:** the Create Record paragraph in `http-protocol.mdx` and the two dogfood pins. The paragraph restates the note's contract without widening it (same doors, same code, same no-naming promise, same deference to best-effort `field`); the pins assert the identity of the answers and the untouched rows at the three HTTP doors, under `private` OWD in one organization and under `isolated` and `group` across two. Consumer and record agree.
- **Execution plan:** none is owed — the amendment accepts a residual and changes no code; "What this binds" names the bar a reversal must clear (import round-trips without an exemption that re-opens the door), which is the bar options a–e failed in code (`import-runner.ts:1243` respects a supplied id; an unheld id answers `201`, so no refusal shape can close the signal — option e). The reasoning holds against the tree.
- **Tried to break it:** (a) a store without a primary key — found, ①.7, qualifier owed, binding sentence survives; (b) a create door that forks on visibility — the per-object batch upsert on `main` does, but it is not a create door for a held id there, and the sibling that makes it one answers this contract — ①.8; (c) a body that differs by holder — `developerMessage` carries object and field labels only; (d) a vacuous wall — the precondition measures it, ①.11.

**Must-fix:** none.
**Should-fix:** (1) ①.7 — one clause naming the store precondition ("on a store that enforces the primary key — every persistent driver; `driver-memory` declares none") in the note's second fact, so the governed text does not state a fact false on a shipped non-production driver; (2) ①.8 — the later of this PR and `claude/harden-upsert-by-id-visibility` names the per-object batch `upsert` arm among the doors, beside import's upsert.

Everything outside the range stands as judged in 6559209282.

### ① Derived judgments

The delta adds one qualifier to the ADR note's second fact and to the page's Create Record paragraph: "on a store that enforces the primary key". Each sentence it introduces, judged:

1. **"the SQL-family drivers do (`driver-sql`, and `driver-sqlite-wasm` and `driver-turso`, which extend it)" — right.** `SqliteWasmDriver extends SqlDriver` (`sqlite-wasm-driver.ts:67`) and `TursoDriver extends SqlDriver` (`turso-driver.ts:1815`). `driver-sql` emits the `id` column as the primary key in its DDL (`sql-driver.ts:10550`, `11091`, `12426` — `table.string('id').primary()`), so every table the family creates refuses a duplicate `id` at the store. `driver-turso` overrides `create` (3026) and `bulkCreate` (3751) for its remote face, but both faces write the same libsql table whose DDL carries that key, and the duplicate's refusal — SQLite's `UNIQUE constraint failed: t.id`, the same sentence a primary-key collision raises — is classified by message (`unique-violation.ts:210`), so the remote face answers the same `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION`. Held on both faces.
2. **"`driver-memory` … declares no primary key, so a duplicate `id` lands there (its docblock in `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts`)" — right.** The docblock at 470-484: "there is no primary key … Two rows with the same `id` still land — through `create` and `bulkCreate` alike, unless `id` itself declares `unique` or a declared index lists it". Cited accurately, and the citation is a position, not a recipe.
3. **The scoping of the claim — right, and no more.** The qualifier names the family that enforces the key and the one store that does not; it says nothing of `driver-mongodb` or `driver-odata`, which is correct silence (mongodb's duplicate-key mapping unmeasured, odata delegating to the remote), and exactly the narrowing the PM seat describes rather than "every persistent driver". The binding sentence ("no create door answers differently by the holder's visibility; none names the holder") is unchanged and still holds on every store, driver-memory included.
4. **Wrong by one appositive (should-fix): "the dev and edge fallback".** Both hunks call `driver-memory` "the dev and edge fallback" (ADR) / "a dev and edge fallback" (page). The repo does not support either word: its README names the driver for "development, unit tests, Storybook, and browser MSW mocks" and marks production ❌ (README lines 3, 83, 87), and the one place "edge" appears there attributes edge deployments to `driver-turso` (line 93). Nothing serves driver-memory as a fallback today — `serve.ts:3349` records that it *used to* build the in-memory driver by default, past tense. The contract clause is accurate; the descriptor is not. One edit: "the development and test driver, not a production store (its README)" — or drop the appositive, since the docblock citation already carries the fact.
5. **Nothing else moved.** Status line, S10 row, the door list, the ruling paragraph, the options, "What this binds", the pins and the vitest entry are byte-identical to the reviewed head; the page's 409 example and the paragraph's remaining sentences are unchanged. Anchors untouched; `Check Documentation Links` green on the head.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `skip-changeset`, no changeset — still correct; the delta touches `docs/adr/**` and `content/docs/**` only. Check-runs at reading: no failure; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (aggregator), `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`, `Flag docs affected`, `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` green; `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Test Core 1-8`, `Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates`, the remaining Lint families and `Live E2E UI` in progress. Landing waits for green per the seat's ② gate.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The flags of 6559209282 stand (harness docblock card; unpinned doors; fleet-write read-back out of scope; dogfood shards skipped on `pull_request` by design; sibling `claude/harden-upsert-by-id-visibility` adds the per-object batch `upsert` door to the list if it lands second — should-fix 2 of that record, not applied by this delta and not owed by it).
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` — no login note.

### ④ Design judgment

The qualifier makes the ADR's recorded fact true on the tree: it names the stores on which the contract is a store-level refusal and the one shipped store on which it is not, without widening the ruling or adding a store the code does not prove. The page restates the same scoping in one clause, consistently with the ADR. The only sentence the delta introduces that the tree does not support is the driver-memory descriptor in ①.4, a characterisation rather than a contract: a should-fix, not a false promise about any door.

**Must-fix:** none.
**Should-fix:** ①.4 — replace "the dev and edge fallback" / "a dev and edge fallback" with what the driver's README says of it (development and tests, not production), in both hunks.
